feature: Role-based model routing research (planner / builder / evaluator)
problem: The harness has three roles — planner, builder, evaluator — each with distinct capability requirements and failure modes. Both planner.md and evaluator.md use model:inherit, giving every role the same model as the builder. This is safe but suboptimal: the evaluator needs anti-sycophancy (favors stronger reasoning models), the planner needs clean decomposition (favors thinking models for complex tasks), and the builder's model is user-controlled. Beyond model selection, it is unresolved whether the planner should remain a subagent or be converted to a skill, and how practitioners configure per-role routing in the IDE.
proposed_solution: Research + decision artifacts only. Extend .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md with: (1) role×tier matrix answering which model tier optimizes outcome-per-cost per role; (2) subagent vs skill analysis for the planner role; (3) workflow integration — how model routing fits into the existing planner→builder→evaluator flow without adding friction; (4) IDE configuration guide — model: frontmatter + harness-model-routing.json + AGENTS.md override path. Also produce tests/eval/fixtures/model_routing_matrix.json as a machine-readable artifact for feat-eval-role-model-matrix.
acceptance_criteria: model-selection.md contains a '## Role × Tier Matrix' section with a table covering planner, builder, and evaluator rows and at minimum columns: role, recommended_tier, fallback_tier, primary_failure_mode, routing_signal: grep -c '## Role' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md && grep -c 'planner\|evaluator\|builder' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md | grep -v '^0$' && echo PASS-AC1

model-selection.md contains a '## Subagent vs Skill' section that gives a binary recommendation (keep as subagent OR convert to skill) for the planner role with explicit rationale referencing Phase 5 S4 counter-evidence: grep -c '## Subagent vs Skill' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md && echo PASS-AC2

model-selection.md contains a '## Workflow Integration' section documenting where model selection decisions occur in the planner→builder→evaluator flow and what (if anything) changes for the practitioner: grep -c '## Workflow Integration' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md && echo PASS-AC3

model-selection.md contains a '## IDE Configuration' section with concrete steps to set per-role models in the IDE (frontmatter path, sync step, override path): grep -c '## IDE Configuration' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md && echo PASS-AC4

tests/eval/fixtures/model_routing_matrix.json exists and is valid JSON with a 'roles' key containing entries for planner, builder, and evaluator, each with recommended_tier, fallback_tier, signals, and scenarios_to_validate fields: python3 -c "import json; m=json.load(open('tests/eval/fixtures/model_routing_matrix.json')); r=m['roles']; assert all(k in r for k in ['planner','builder','evaluator']); assert all('recommended_tier' in r[k] and 'scenarios_to_validate' in r[k] for k in r); print('PASS-AC5')"
edge_cases: Planner subagent vs skill analysis must engage Phase 5 S4 counter-evidence (S4 argues skills-over-agents for most cases, with evaluator as the exception) — not just assert a conclusion

IDE Configuration section must address the sync step (make sync-local copies library/ to .cursor/agents/) — recommending a frontmatter change without mentioning sync would leave the practitioner with a stale config
model_routing_matrix.json must not hardcode volatile model IDs (gpt-5.5, claude-*) as recommended_tier values — use tier labels (fast, balanced, reasoning) with example model IDs listed separately
